note: both apps render these same questions; regenerate, never hand-edit

questions.title: How should Jarvis talk?
questions.help: This changes only how answers are worded. It never changes what Jarvis does or what it asks you first.

options.label: Warm and brief (default)
options.detail: Friendly and short, like a helpful person.

options.label: Plain
options.detail: Neutral and businesslike - just the answer.

questions.title: Should Jarvis use a little humour?
questions.help: Occasional light humour when it fits. Never on cards, errors, or serious topics.

questions.title: How careful should Jarvis be before it acts?
questions.help: Which of your things Jarvis may read, and whether it asks first. Making it MORE careful happens at once; making it LESS careful asks you on its own card, one for each thing.

options.label: Strict - ask me first for all seven
options.detail: Calendar, email, notes, home status, and writing to Obsidian, Logseq and Joplin: always ask first.

options.label: Balanced - leave my current first-time choices alone
options.detail: The setup changes none of the "what asks first" rows; you can see and change them in Settings, What asks first.

options.label: Trusting - go ahead without a card
options.detail: Jarvis may read and write those seven without asking. Each one still asks you on its own card before it changes, and it can only be changed from the PC.

questions.title: How should Jarvis learn?
questions.help: Facts about you and your projects are learned from YOUR own words only. Turning learning on, or letting sensitive topics be learned automatically, asks you on a card. Turning things off is instant.

options.label: Learn automatically (recommended)
options.detail: Facts are saved without a per-fact yes; sensitive topics still wait for your yes.

options.label: Learn automatically, including sensitive topics
options.detail: Health, money and private details about other people are also saved without asking. Turning this on raises its own card.

options.label: Don't learn automatically; ask me for each fact

questions.title: Which of your things may the AI model read when you ask?
questions.help: These are the tools Jarvis may be offered at all. Turning one on shows its own approval card and asks for Windows Hello, on the PC; turning one off is instant. All / None applies to the whole list.

questions.title: Should Jarvis be able to search the web?
questions.help: A search still shows its exact words on a card first when private things could slip in. Turning web search on raises its one card; turning it off is instant.

options.label: Yes, search the web when it helps

questions.title: How often should Jarvis ask before a web search?
questions.help: By default a search asks only when it could include something private. Asking before EVERY search is stricter and instant; turning that back off raises a card.

options.label: Ask only when private things could slip in (default)

questions.title: Which search service should Jarvis use?
questions.help: The service only sees the words of a search Jarvis decides to make. Some need a key you add later in Settings; changing this is instant.

options.label: SearXNG on this PC (default, no key)
Brave Search (needs a key and a card)

questions.title: What may Jarvis look at or draw on this PC?
questions.help: Each of these has its own existing card or switch. Picture mode and the headless browser each raise their own card when turned on. All / None applies to the whole list.

options.label: Picture mode - read the words on my screen
Let me ask Jarvis to make pictures
Data and maths sandbox (small Python runs)

questions.title: Which notifications do you want?
questions.help: Each switch only changes when this PC or your phone speaks up; none of them raises a card, and none of them is ever a way out of your own devices. All / None applies to the whole list.

options.label: Show who new emails are from in the morning briefing
A notification when the briefing is ready

questions.title: How much of an approval card should be shown at first?
questions.help: This only changes how much of the card is open when it appears: the same card, the same words underneath, the same buttons. Instant either way.

questions.title: Which voice options should be on?
questions.help: These only change how Jarvis sounds. This questionnaire never starts voice training - that stays your own step, in Settings. All / None applies to the whole list.

options.label: Better voice on the second card
options.detail: Turning this on raises its own card, and needs a second card.

questions.title: How should the animal faces behave?
questions.help: Small cosmetic switches, shared by the PC and the phone. None of them raises a card. All / None applies to the whole list.

options.label: Show the sun and moon behind the face

questions.title: What will you mostly use Jarvis for?
questions.help: This recommends one of the existing work presets. It changes NO model by itself: a preset is only applied by choosing it in the preset selector, where its own ONE card asks you.

options.label: Everyday questions, writing and life admin
Coding and long jobs with tools
Using websites and filling in forms, step by step

questions.title: Which personality should Jarvis have?
questions.help: The personality changes how Jarvis words things - its tone and character - and nothing else: not what it does, not what it asks you first, and no approval card. It is the same choice the Personality control in Settings makes.

options.label: Warm Collaborator
options.detail: Friendly and on your side - the default.

options.label: Classic British Butler
options.detail: Formal, precise and discreet.

options.label: Tactical Mission Control
options.detail: Short, clipped and operational.

options.label: Dry & Deadpan
options.detail: Understated humour, never at your expense.

options.label: Sharp Tech Partner
options.detail: Direct, technical and quick to the point.

options.label: Socratic Coach & Tutor
options.detail: Asks the next question and teaches as it goes.

options.label: No-Nonsense Critic
options.detail: Finds the weak spot and says so plainly.

options.label: Calm & Grounded
options.detail: Steady and unhurried, even under pressure.

options.label: Patient Advocate
options.detail: Takes your side and explains the options.

options.label: Reflective Coach
options.detail: Helps you think it through before deciding.

questions.title: Should Jarvis avoid AI-sounding writing?
questions.help: The Anti-Slop filter takes out the phrases that make writing sound machine-made. It changes only the words, so neither direction asks on a card. "During" filters as Jarvis writes; "after" audits the answer and lists what it would change instead.

options.label: No, leave the writing as it is (default)
Yes, filter it as Jarvis writes
options.detail: The filter works while the answer is written.

options.label: Yes, but only list what it would change first
options.detail: Jarvis answers normally, then audits its own wording.

questions.title: May Jarvis switch lights, plugs and fans without a card?
questions.help: On means a light, plug or fan in your home can be switched without a card each time. Turning that on raises ONE approval card first; turning it back off is instant. Nothing else in your home changes.

options.label: Yes, switch them without a card each time
options.detail: Turning this on raises its own card once.

options.label: No, ask me first every time (default)

questions.title: Should Jarvis save a fact when it had to reword it?
questions.help: Facts are normally learned from your own words. With this on, Jarvis may also save a fact whose words are its own - which is how it can keep something you implied rather than said. Off by default; turning it on raises its own card.

options.label: Yes, save a reworded fact too
options.detail: Turning this on raises its own card once.

questions.title: Should Jarvis keep your chats and voice transcripts on this PC?
questions.help: On keeps the conversation on this PC so Jarvis can pick it up later; it is kept encrypted. Off means nothing is written. Turning it back on raises its own card; turning it off is instant.

options.label: Yes, keep them on this PC (default)

questions.title: Should recordings and videos be searchable by their words?
questions.help: On keeps readable words from recordings and videos in the folders you listed, so Jarvis can find them later. Off stops keeping them and is instant; turning it back on raises its own card.

options.label: No, do not keep their words

questions.title: Should the small approvals ask for your fingerprint too?
questions.help: A small read-only card - a web search, a page, the news - can be approved by the card alone, or every card can ask for your fingerprint as well. Turning the fingerprint on is instant; turning it off can only be done on this PC.

options.label: Yes, ask for my fingerprint on the small cards too
No, the card alone is enough (default)
options.detail: This can only be chosen on the PC itself.

questions.title: How fast should Jarvis speak?
questions.help: This only changes how fast spoken answers are read. It never changes what Jarvis says, and no card either way.

questions.title: Should Jarvis say "One moment" while it thinks?
questions.help: The short spoken line before a slower answer. Off hides it everywhere both apps speak, and no card either way.

options.label: No, stay quiet while it thinks

questions.title: How long should Jarvis Live wait before it turns itself off?
questions.help: How long Live keeps listening after it last hears you. This never starts Live and never opens the microphone; no card either way.

questions.title: Should Jarvis offer the bigger model when it would help?
questions.help: These only decide whether Jarvis OFFERS a bigger model at a moment it might help. Every offer still needs your yes, and no model is switched by this answer. All / None applies to the whole list.

options.label: When I seem to be struggling
